title: Australia’s social media ban six months later

paragraphs: Australia has a new law since December. This law says that children under 16 cannot use social media like YouTube or Instagram. The government wants to help kids feel better.

But the law is not working. Many children still use these apps every day. It is very easy to make a new account. Children can just write a false age, or their parents can help them. The big computer companies do not stop the children.
Now, the government is angry. They want these companies to pay a lot of money if they do not follow the rules. Other countries are looking at Australia to see what happens next.

words.d: the people who control a country

paragraphs: An ambitious Australian law, which came into effect last December to protect youth mental health, bans children under 16 from having social media accounts. However, half a year later, studies show the ban is largely ineffective.

Most underage users can easily access and create new accounts on platforms like Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube. Although the government recommends strict verification steps, tech companies mostly rely on simple self-declarations of age that children can easily bypass. Sometimes, children ask their parents to complete face verification for them, or they continue using their old, unverified accounts. Furthermore, software designed to estimate a user’s age based on online activity rarely works.

In response to this non-compliance, the Australian government has doubled the maximum fines for tech giants and warned them of potential court action. Despite these early struggles, countries around the world, including the EU, are closely watching Australia’s progress as they consider implementing similar bans.

paragraphs: In December, Australia started a new law that stops children under 16 from using social media. The government wanted to protect the mental health of young people. But six months later, the law is not working well.

Studies show that most kids can still easily open and use accounts on Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube. The tech companies don’t check the age of their users carefully. Children can lie about their age, or they can ask their parents to help them pass the face checks. The special computer programs which try to guess a user’s age don’t work well either.

Now, the government is very angry with the big tech companies. They doubled the fines for companies which don’t follow the rules. Other countries in the world are watching Australia to see if they should make similar laws.
